summary_for_children: Al-'Asr means Time. It says all people are in loss except those who believe, do good, and remind each other of truth and patience.
environment_concept: A world built inside the flow of time: sand pouring from a vast hourglass across a dune landscape, and four keys that save from loss: faith, good deeds, advising truth and advising patience.
architecture_and_scenery: A huge hourglass on a dune plain, a sundial, four gates.

depiction_rules: No prophet, person or representation of Allah is shown. Unseen realities are never pictured. Interactive activities are labelled as adaptations.

unique_world.visual_theme: A small hill town in the late afternoon with a mosque, a grocer, a well and a green, the sun already low

primary_mechanic.text: Before a 120-second sunset, do the four things 103:3 names at four places: pray the afternoon prayer (believe), carry water for an old neighbour (do good), tell the grocer his scale reads short (urge the truth), sit with a friend whose kite broke (urge patience). A juggler, a gossip bench and marbles each spend 50 seconds; if the sun sets first, the afternoon is lost and the four start over. The sky reddens as time runs out.

unique_world.narrative_structure: A reading above the town, the afternoon, then a reading on the green
environment_behaviour: the light turns from golden to red as the afternoon runs out
unique_world.learning_objective: Know the four things that save from loss: faith, good deeds, urging truth and urging patience (103:3)

story_library.title: The Treasure of Time
story_library.children_narration: Time passes whether we notice it or not. Surah Al-Asr reminds us that faith, good actions, truth, and patience are essential. Every day gives us opportunities to do something meaningful.

world_idea.title: The Clockwork World
world_idea.description: Explore giant moving clock mechanisms and arrange a fictional day's activities to learn about balancing responsibilities and helping others.
